claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into both operands of every SqlBinaryExpression with no OperatorType filter, so AndAlso/OrElse operands are wrongly treated as null-propagating and a load-bearing IS NOT NULL guard is dropped, producing silently wrong query results.
raw:
### C1 — `AndAlso`/`OrElse` are not null-propagating; their operands are harvested anyway

`SqlBinaryExpression.IsValidOperator` (`SqlBinaryExpression.cs:93,95,102`) admits `AndAlso`, `OrElse`, and `Coalesce`. Under SQL three-valued logic `NULL AND FALSE = FALSE` and `NULL OR TRUE = TRUE` — the optimization's invariant ("operand IS NULL ⟹ result IS NULL") does not hold, so a load-bearing `IS NOT NULL` check gets dropped.

claim: Binary Coalesce is also admitted by the unfiltered recursion and should be excluded defensively; EF's own factory emits Coalesce as a SqlFunctionExpression so it is not reachable today, but a provider could construct the binary node.
raw: *(`Coalesce` is defensive only: `SqlExpressionFactory.Coalesce` at line 502-508 emits a `SqlFunctionExpression` with `argumentsPropagateNullability: [false, false]`, which the function branch handles correctly. But binary `Coalesce` is a legal node a provider could construct.)*

claim: For comparison operators and boolean Not the result is a search condition whose NULL operand yields UNKNOWN, not NULL, so once the CASE guard is dropped SQL Server's SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor re-wraps it with no ELSE NULL arm and UNKNOWN collapses to false.
raw:
### C2 — Comparison results are search conditions: `UNKNOWN` becomes `false`, not `NULL`

For `Equal`/`NotEqual`/`LessThan`/… a NULL operand yields `UNKNOWN`, not a NULL *value*. That distinction is invisible while the condition sits inside `CASE WHEN … THEN <cond> ELSE NULL END`. Once the guard is dropped, SQL Server's `SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor` re-wraps the bare condition as a value with **no `ELSE NULL` arm**, so `UNKNOWN` collapses to `0`.

claim: None of the five new tests places a logical connective or a comparison in the CASE result — only shapes where dropping the check is correct — so the suite passes identically with or without a fix for the unsound path, and many branches (Negate, arithmetic/bitwise operators, the ArgumentsPropagateNullability false guard, InstancePropagatesNullability, DropNotNullChecks' right-dropped and binary.Update arms, OrElse in test position) are untested.
raw:
### H3 — No test covers a boolean or comparison result, which is exactly the unsound path

All five new tests use `~A` (bitwise `Not`), int `Add`, or string concat. Every one is a shape where dropping the check is *correct*. Nothing places a logical connective or a comparison in the **result** — `Is_not_null_optimizes_binary_op_with_mixed_checks` (2290) puts `x.BoolA` in the *test*, never the result. **The suite passes identically with or without a fix for C1/C2.**

claim: clause.Result is visited with preserveColumnNullabilityInformation: true, so it has already been simplified under the very non-null assumption the guard establishes; hoisting it out of the guard is what makes the optimization unsound, and the must-propagate invariant is written down nowhere.
raw:
### M4 — The result was simplified under the very assumption being dropped

`clause.Result` is visited with `preserveColumnNullabilityInformation: true` (line 511-518), so the test's columns are in `_nonNullableColumns` while the result is being rewritten. Directly observable: on base, `A == B` inside the guard emits `A = B AND B IS NOT NULL` — the `A IS NOT NULL` conjunct is *missing because it was assumed*. Hoisting that expression out of the guard is what makes C1 unsound rather than merely over-eager.

claim: Both null-propagation helpers are static local functions inside VisitCase, so providers with custom null-propagating node types have no protected virtual seam to participate and would have to fork all of VisitCase.
raw:
### M5 — No provider extension point for the new null-propagation model

Both helpers are `static` local functions inside `VisitCase`. Every other nullability decision in this class is `protected virtual`, and providers already use that seam — `SqlServerSqlNullabilityProcessor.VisitCustomSqlExpression:37` and `SqliteSqlNullabilityProcessor:36` both handle custom node types that propagate NULL from their operands and are invisible to this model.

claim: Base-class expression types the processor already visits (AtTimeZone, Collate, Distinct, JsonScalar) are absent from the null-propagation model, so the optimization silently misses them.
raw: Base-class types the class already visits are missing too (`VisitAtTimeZone:479`, `VisitCollate:659`, `VisitDistinct:689`, `VisitJsonScalar:1615`) — missed optimizations only, but the drift is structural. Promote to `protected virtual void CollectNullPropagatedOperands(...)` with a `base` fall-through.

claim: The entire result subtree is walked into a HashSet<SqlExpression> before DropNotNullChecks establishes that the test contains any IS NOT NULL at all, so the work repeats per nested CASE and is pure waste when the test is an unrelated predicate.
raw:
### M6 — Operand set is built before it can possibly be useful

The full result subtree is walked into a `HashSet<SqlExpression>` (structural `Equals`/`GetHashCode` per node) *before* `DropNotNullChecks` establishes that `clause.Test` contains even one `IS NOT NULL`. `VisitCase` recurses across the whole SQL tree, so this repeats per nested `CASE` and is pure waste whenever the test is an unrelated predicate. Scan the test first and bail early.

raw: **M5. Hashing cost.** `HashSet<SqlExpression>` hashes whole subtrees, and `NullPropagatedOperands` inserts every node on the null-propagating spine, so the collection pass is O(n²) in subtree size for deep expressions. Irrelevant for typical trees; worth a thought if this ever runs on machine-generated queries.

claim: The analysis recurses by node type and filters by operator only for SqlUnaryExpression, so a newly permitted binary operator becomes silently unsound instead of failing closed; it should be an explicit operator allowlist with a default: return.
raw: 1. **Invert the analysis from "which nodes do I recurse into" to "which operators are on an explicit allowlist."** The current code recurses by node *type* (`SqlBinaryExpression`) and filters by operator only for `SqlUnaryExpression`. Making the binary case operator-driven, with a `default: return;`, means a newly-permitted operator fails closed instead of silently unsound.

claim: The soundness contract NullPropagatedOperands is asserting is never stated in a comment, and the unstated third clause (after search-condition conversion) is the one C2 violates.
raw: 2. **State the soundness contract in a comment** on `NullPropagatedOperands`: "*`expression` evaluates to NULL whenever any collected operand is NULL — in value semantics, in every provider, after search-condition conversion.*" All three clauses matter, and C2 is a violation of the third one that reads correct if you only think about clause one.
